minane bridge – fri 6th: 11am, minane bridge (change of time) – sat 7th: 7.30pm, minane bridge – sun 8th: 11.15am, nohoval – mon 9th & tues 10th: 7.30pm, nohoval. prayer petitions may be left in either church or with the sacristans. mass of remembrance — sunday 8th november at 11.15am in st. patrick’s church, nohoval. bereaved families are wa rmly invited to this special mass, with music by dan twomey and the choir. tracton athletic club — congratulations to all who took part in last sunday’s dublin city marathon. well done!our confirmation ceremony for 2027 will take place on monday, april 12th. due to exceptionally large numbers this year, the ceremony will take place in carrigaline church. following a parent vote to decide the best path forward, moving to a larger venue ensures that everyone, parents, grandparents, sponsors, siblings and extended family can attend comfortably . please note that this venue change is just for this year due to large numbers. all preparation confirmation masses over t he coming months will take place here in our own parish as no rmal. weekend masses — sat: 7pm, shanbally. sunday: 8.45am, the oratory (1st & 3rd sundays only) – 10am, fridays, 6–7pm. novena to the holy souls — 2nd–10th november across all four churches, including during funerals. additional 10am masses: monday 2nd, monkstown – monday 9th, passage west. blessing of graves — sun 1st nov: st james cemetery, chetwynd, togher, 3pm. sun 8th nov: barnahely, 2pm – old chur ch, 3pm – new cemetery, passage west, 4pm. confirmation 2027 — passage west: 11th february – monkstown: 1st march. fr. james will share a beekeeping talk tuesday evening (nov 3rd) at 7.30pm in the parish centre. there will be a safe observation beebox to see the bees up close, what bees do and how they work in total harmony, honey tasting and more! no charge but please give your name into the sacristy or parish office as numbers will be limited. it will be over at 9pm followed by a cup of tea november novena runs from monday nov 2nd to tuesday nov 10th with mass at 9.30am and 7.30pm each weekd ay. prayers and blessing of graves at 3pm in st mary’s cemetery on sunday nov 8th tue. 3rd 10:00am holy souls novena wed. 4th 10:00am holy souls novena thurs. 5th 10:00am holy souls novena fri. 6th 10:00am holy souls novena we rememb er all those who died recently. bereavement /remembrance mass the bereavement mass will be celebrated on monday november 2nd at 7:30pm, all souls day. this mass is for all those who have died in the past year and an opportunity for their families to remember them with the parish community. there will be a candle with the name of each person who has died at the back of the church on the evening of the mass and also some extra candles for anyone who wishes to remember a loved one during this bereavement service. cleaning our church like any building, needs regular cleaning and it has been the tradition in this parish that volunteers clean the church weekly. we are grateful to all those who, over many years have generously given of their time to meet this ministry. we appeal each year for volunteers, (male and female) but it is a challenge to find parishioners eager to serve this ministry. the church cleaning task takes one hour on a saturday morning. we currently have 2 teams which means each team does one hour every 2 weeks. if you can help, please contact the parish office. thank you. thursday coffee mornings after 10:00am mass. all welcome . choir: as always, new members are very welcome. practice is on tuesday nights from 7:30 – 9:00pm. blessing of the graves the blessing of the graves will be held on november 1st at 3:00pm in st. james cemetery, chetwynd, togher. you are all very welcome to attend. ireland's 3rd national first saturdays conference this year's conference will take place in knock on saturday november 28th. the day begins at 10am and finishes at 5pm. it includes holy mass, adoration, talks, and a healing service. speakers include: fr patrick cahill, geraldine o'donnell, fr leon pereira op, nikki kingsley, fr marius o'reilly, fr. jaimie twohig, christine o'hara, fr. mark
